V1695500895.title: Knotboard
V1695500895.content:
001  
Knotboard —AI-Powered SaaS for Creative Workflows
 Exit Page  

Knotboard


Designed  a connected creative SaaS workspace that turns inspiration into action — helping creatives capture ideas, build projects, track progress, and uncover patterns across their creative process.

ROLE

PRODUCT DESIGNER
BRAND DESIGNERSCOPE

UIUX Design
Visual Design
Design Engineer

｜W38 Task Management +46 XP  ｜W38 Inspiration/File Auto Categorized +20 XP ｜W37 Project Planning +28  XP ｜W36 Productivity&Creativity +30  XP ｜W 35 Weekly Reflection Routine +34XP

 Overview& Context  

Connect ideas, plans, files, and learning in one creative flow.


A designer may save a reference on Instagram, write a thought in Notes, plan the week in a calendar, track tasks in another app, and export the final file into a folder. Each tool works on its own. The problem appears between them. Context disappears during every handoff, and the creator must rebuild the story of the work from memory.

Knotboard brings that story into one connected workspace. A reference can become a task. A task can belong to a project, appear in the weekly plan, move onto a calendar, produce a deliverable, and return to the dashboard as evidence for reflection. The product keeps the source, action, output, and learning connected.





 The Problem  


Creative work fails when ideas and execution stay disconnected？


Imagine a design student named Maya. On Monday, she saves a typographic poster because of its unusual grid. On Tuesday, she finds a material experiment in a gallery archive. By Friday, both references are buried under newer images. When she begins her own project, she remembers that she found something useful, but not where it came from or why it mattered.

The missing feature is not another bookmark. Maya needs a path from recognition to action. She needs to record the reason a reference matters, connect it to a project, and decide what to do with it while the thought is still fresh.



The opportunity


The product opportunity was to treat creative work as a connected cycle instead of a set of isolated lists. Inspiration should carry its context forward. Planning should be flexible enough for exploratory work. Completion should recognize output without forcing every task to produce a file. Review should turn activity into an informed next step.



  User Research  

Different roles share the same broken handoffs.


Knotboard focuses first on individual creators, but the system was designed around needs that also appear in fast-moving content work and design teams. The details change by role; the underlying job remains consistent: keep ideas, commitments, and evidence of progress connected.


These behaviors led to a central design principle: Knotboard should reduce the cost of moving from one stage of work to the next. The system should remember the relationships so the user can keep thinking about the work itself.



                                        




  Basic Fucntion  





  Inspiration  


Capture first, organize when the idea has a future.


The Inspiration library is the product’s front door. It accepts the messy forms in which ideas actually arrive: a URL, an image, a sentence, a PDF, or another file. The capture field stays prominent and lightweight because adding a reference should not require a classification decision first.




Why the library behaves differently from a folder


Knotboard stores more than files—it preserves why each reference matters and what it could become. Users can organize items, connect them to projects, and turn them into tasks without losing context. Compact URL cards, visual-first image cards, and hidden drag controls keep the library flexible and uncluttered.







  Planner  

 

A plan should give shape to the week without pretending every task is predictable


Creative work contains different kinds of effort. Some tasks are routine and easy to estimate. Others are uncertain because the creator is still learning what the problem is. Knotboard makes that difference visible without turning planning into a scoring exercise.


One task, several useful views


Planner, Calendar, Tasks, and Project pages do not create separate copies of a task. They show the same record from different angles. The Planner supports weekly intent. Calendar handles dated work and a backlog. Tasks provides a searchable operational list. Projects preserve context and history. Editing status, due date, estimate, or assignment in one view updates the same underlying task everywhere.






  Project& Channel  


The project page keeps the work and the evidence together


A creative project is more than a task list. It has a reason, a body of research, a changing plan, and artifacts that show what was made. Knotboard’s Channel and Project structure keeps those layers in one place without forcing every project into the same template.



Channels create a stable map


Channel organize the larger areas of a creative practice. Each channel contains projects. Each project can hold its own tasks, inspiration, description, link, cover, status, and deliverables. This structure lets a user zoom from a long-term area of growth to the exact task that needs attention today.




Deliverables make progress visible


When a task produces an image, document, link, or other output, the result appears in the project’s Deliverables gallery. The gallery is both practical and motivational: it creates a visual record of work that would otherwise vanish into folders. Because deliverables are optional, the system respects tasks whose value is learning, deciding, communicating, or exploring.




Points reward effort without replacing judgment


Points translate task difficulty, importance, output value, and time into a lightweight signal. They help users compare commitments and recognize effort. They are not a quality score. The product pairs them with the actual deliverable and a written reflection so progress is never reduced to a number.







   Dashboard    


Completion becomes useful when it changes the next plan


Most productivity tools treat completion as the end of the story. Knotboard treats it as evidence. The Dashboard gathers completed tasks, time, points, project status, deliverables, and review notes into one place. A global time filter keeps the period consistent across charts so users do not have to reconcile daily, weekly, monthly, and overall views by hand.





   Knot AI Agent    

AI Agent appears where context already exists



Knot Agent is not a separate chatbot pasted onto the product. Its usefulness depends on the workspace around it: saved references, unfinished tasks, project priorities, dates, estimates, deliverables, and review history. The agent can make a relevant suggestion because Knotboard has preserved the context of the work.












  Reflection  


Designing the system changed how I define productivity


At the start, Knotboard could have become a larger to-do list. The research framing and product structure pushed it in a different direction. Creative productivity depends on preserving meaning across time. The reference that sparked the work, the decision that shaped the plan, the effort required to make it, and the lesson discovered afterward all belong to the same story.

The project strengthened my ability to work across product strategy and visual design. Information architecture made the system coherent. Interaction design made the handoffs usable. The visual language made a dense workspace feel calm. Brand thinking gave the product a clear point of view. AI design added a new constraint: assistance is valuable only when it uses context responsibly and keeps the user’s judgment visible.

O4158167021.title: Reelshort Casting System
O4158167021.content:
002  
ReelShort Casting System — Casting at 100M+ View Scale
  Exit Page   


Reelshort Casting System




A casting management system designed for a leading short-form drama platform with billions of views, streamlining how production teams discover, evaluate, and manage talent across fast-paced productions.

ROLE

PRODUCT DESIGNER
BRAND DESIGNERSCOPE

Product  Design
User  Experience Research
Design Engineer  




 Overview  

ReelShort produces a high volume of short-form dramas every year, which means casting teams constantly need to find, evaluate, and coordinate with a large pool of actors.

The existing Casting Hub helped centralize this process, but finding the right talent still required navigating dense profiles, incomplete information, multiple platforms, and repetitive communication.

I redesigned the platform around one goal: Make casting decisions faster with less manual work.


 




  The Problem  

Imagine you are a producer/casting director casting a new short drama.You need to search for actors across IMDb, Instagram, agencies, and internal records.  Then you compare photos, check availability and location, organize contact information, reach out, and track responses.

A lot of time is spent simply collecting information before a casting decision can even happen.The opportunity was to turn the Casting Hub from a talent database into a more useful decision-making tool.






  User Research  

Before redesigning the platform, I wanted to understand what casting professionals actually pay attention to. I did research with five Producers and Casting Directors working across short-form entertainment and fashion about how they find talent, compare candidates, and make final decisions.

I spoke with five Producers and Casting Directors working across short-form entertainment and fashion. Four needs came up repeatedly: Visual Fit, Complete Information, Chemistry, Agency Network. These insights became the foundation of the redesign.





  Key Design Decisions  

(All data shown is fictional demo data for demonstration reason. Real user data is strictly protected and will not be displayed.)

  01 · Make Talent Card More Visual  

Multiple photos can be viewed directly from the card, while the information hierarchy prioritizes the details needed for quick decisions. Casting teams can screen talent from the grid and open fewer profiles along the way.





   

  

 02 · Surface Information Completeness   

I identified 12 key data points commonly needed during casting and introduced a Profile Completeness indicator. Casting teams can quickly see which profiles are ready for consideration and which are missing critical information.





  03 · Rebuild Agency Library Page  

I redesigned the Agency Library to connect agencies directly with the actors they represent.  Casting teams can move between an agency, its contacts, and its talent pool without treating them as separate databases.







  04 · Change the Filter’s Information Architecture  

The original filter offered comprehensive options, but the structure was cluttered and single-select interactions made complex searches inefficient.
I reorganized the hierarchy, merged overlapping criteria, removed unnecessary options, and introduced multi-select filtering.A cleaner, more flexible filtering experience helps casting teams narrow down talent faster.







  05 · VFX Information UI  System’s  Update  

The VFX grading standard is the reference the team uses to grade every project's visual effects, from D (simple shot) to S+ (top-tier difficulty).  
I turned the old full-width table into a collapsible card with colour-coded grade chips, a lighter table and a short pricing footnote. The project list now sits near the top of the VFX page, and the full standards are still one click away.







 Outcome  

Casting looks like picking faces, but most of it is keeping track of information. One role can mean hundreds of actors, each with photos, measurements, an agency, consent limits and a schedule. Before the ReelShort Casting Hub, all of that lived in spreadsheets, inboxes and people's memory. I designed the hub to bring it into one place.
The hub now holds 600+ actors, 130+ agencies and 60+ projects, and it has become part of a larger internal system. It didn't replace casting judgment. It put everything the team needs in front of them.

I0266811399.content:
003  
Cave Song- Cultural Heritage Preservance App
  Exit Page   


Cave Song



Cave Songs is a digital platform for Dunhuang’s Mogao Caves, bringing together heritage preservation, cultural education, exhibitions and news, digital exploration, and cultural products in one experience.
Part of the Project from Columbia Digital Storytelling Lab.


ROLE

PRODUCT DESIGNER
BRAND DESIGNERSCOPE

UIUX Design
Visual Design
Design Engineer
























INTRODUCTION

This website explores the Mogao Caves through an interactive digital experience that blends cultural heritage, education, and immersive storytelling. By combining visual archives, Buddhist philosophy, historical narratives, and game-inspired interactions, the platform reimagines how audiences engage with ancient Dunhuang art in the contemporary digital age.

Users are invited to virtually navigate cave spaces, uncover hidden stories, restore fragmented murals, and interact with symbolic elements inspired by Buddhist aesthetics and Silk Road history. Through sound, image, and exploration, the project transforms cultural learning into an intuitive and emotionally engaging journey.

Rather than functioning solely as an archive, the website acts as a living digital environment — one that bridges preservation, participation, and contemporary media design.

Somniloquy








SCOPE
Interactive Game  Design, Creative  Direction,
AIGC  Design, 3D  Modeling

ROLE
CREATIVE  DIRECTOR, PRODUCT  DESIGNER
VISUAL  ARTIST



INTRODUCTION

Somniloquy unfolds as a poetic dialogue between sound, image, and the liminal space of the body. Guided by the poems and videos, the performance drifts between consciousness and dream, where spoken language dissolves into sonic vibration.
As one artist weaves a landscape of moving images and ambient sound, the other responds through poetry reading and the ethereal voice of the theremin. Their interaction takes place upon a bed—an intimate stage that evokes memory, sleep, and the fragile border between presence and absence. Lasting ten minutes, the piece invites the audience into a shared reverie, concluding with a five-minute guided meditation that extends the dream beyond the performance itself.


















Prensent at “Pixelated Dream” at the gallery Accent Sisters in New York City, 
Collaborate with Poet Hongru Pan.

T4133279435.title: Vibe Painting
T4133279435.content:
> Next Project  
   Exit ×  


“Vibe Painting” (2026)
Interaction Design  / Creative  Technology

GAME / INTERACTION FUNCTIONS


1. Breath Interaction
Participants can blow toward the camera or microphone to generate expanding clouds of color and fluid particle diffusion.
Different breathing intensities affect the scale, speed, and emotional density of the visual output.
Visual Effects
  • Dynamic color blooming
  • Ink/water diffusion simulation
  • Floating particles
  • Atmospheric motion fields
2. Finger Gesture Interaction
Hand and finger tracking allow users to directly manipulate visual materials in space.
Functions
  • Push and drag particles
  • Blend colors like liquid paint
  • Generate ripple distortions
  • Create motion trails and fluid deformation

3. Blink Recognition
Eye blinking triggers hidden symbolic elements within the system.

Depending on the selected mode:
  • blinking generates stars,
  • floating numerical symbols,
  • or hidden visual fragments.

This mechanism transforms unconscious bodily behavior into poetic digital output, emphasizing the relationship between attention, awareness, and machine perception.4. Mood-Based Color System
The project includes a customizable emotional palette system inspired by:
  • Morandi colors,
  • pastel gradients,
  • natural elements,
  • and AI-generated atmospheric color mapping.

Participants can influence the emotional tone of the environment through simple prompts or interaction patterns.

5. Finish & Save System
At the end of each session, the system freezes the generative canvas and transforms it into a final “Vibe Painting” poster.

The output acts as:
  • a memory trace,
  • emotional snapshot,
  • or digital self-portrait generated through interaction.



 



    






TECHNOLOGY USED



COMPUTER VISION

  • MediaPipe Hand Tracking
  • Face Landmark Detection
  • Blink Detection Algorithms
  • Real-Time Motion Tracking
GENERATIVE VISUAL SYSTEM

  • Particle Systems
  • Fluid Simulation
  • Procedural Animation
  • Noise & Motion Field Generation

CREATIVE CODING & RENDERING

  • JavaScript
  • HTML/CSS
  • Canvas API
  • Three.js / WebGL
  • React & React Three Fiber (R3F)
AI/ INTERACTIVE SYSTEMS

  • AI-assisted visual generation workflows(Gemini 3)
  • Real-time interaction mapping
  • Emotional parameter systems
  • Generative behavior design










ROLE

Creative Technologist
Interaction Designer


INTRODUCTION

Vibe Painting is an AI-driven interactive visual system that transforms human gestures, breath, blinking, and subtle bodily movements into real-time generative imagery.

Positioned between game, installation, and emotional interface, the project explores how invisible human emotions can be translated into fluid digital landscapes through computer vision and generative systems. Rather than functioning as a traditional game with fixed goals, Vibe Painting creates an open-ended sensory experience where participants “paint” using their body, mood, and presence.

Through blowing, finger movement, eye blinking, and spatial interaction, colors, particles, stars, numbers, and abstract visual elements continuously emerge, dissolve, and reorganize on screen — forming a living emotional canvas that is never repeated twice.

Inspired by meditation practices, emotional computing, East Asian aesthetics, and generative art, the system treats interaction not as command, but as a process of resonance between human perception and machine interpretation.

G3448313462.title: A Semiotic Study on Iching
G3448313462.content:
“A Semiotic Study on Iching” (2024)
Interactive Installation/Generative Art/Video Installation

INTRODUCTION

Being an enthusiast of classical Chinese culture, I am fascinated by the philosophy of the I Ching. By generating eight basic elements through the combination of two yin and yang symbols, The I Ching forms sixty-four hexagrams which provides a tool for understanding the world. However, from a literary perspective, the I Ching is a genre of writing that utilizes symbols, guided by visual logic that is not perceived as sacred, inevitable, or unchangeable. It is not a stone tablet left by gods or extraterrestrials but a creation of humans. It possesses a recognizable logic, a comprehensible, and even replicable creative process. To me, it is an open framework. 

In my attempt to create this project, I have rewritten and expanded upon the I Ching within this framework and aim to make its original/contemporary meaning accessible to more people through sound visualizations by coding language,p5js. 

In this project,I take the natural sound tracks represented by the I Ching Bagua to visualize them as images and vibrating lines in coding language P5js.






Procedures：

Step 1: 
Record the sounds of eight natural elements in nature, each corresponding to one of the eight trigrams in the I Ching.Step 2: 
Import the recorded sounds into p5.js.Step 3: 
Use p5.js to visualize the eight natural sounds as generative images that reflect the characteristics of each natural element. All visuals are generated using algorithmic data.Step 4: 
Create an individual audio track for each natural sound.Step 5: 
Pair the visualized sound images in every possible combination (8 × 8 = 64) to depict specific natural scenes.

C3066820907.title: The Museum of Unmourned Things
C3066820907.content:
“The Museum of Unmourned Things” (2025)
Book Design












ROLE

Photographer
Layout Designer



INTRODUCTION

“The Museum (ice-cube) of Unmourned Things” is a poetry-photography project by photographer Jingyi Zhang and poet Lifei Cheng, curator/researcher Ann Wang. Emerging from shared memories across East Asia and the Americas, the project explores impermanence, femininity, grief, desire, and the emotional residues left within landscapes, weather, and everyday objects.

I contributed photographic works, visual sequencing, image-text composition, and publication layout design, shaping the relationship between poetry and image through spatial arrangement and editorial structure. Through the interplay of text, typography, and photography, the project creates a form of visual dialogue where poems and images continuously reflect, interrupt, and reframe one another.

Conceived as both publication and exhibition, the work unfolds as a drifting archive — mapping an intimate topography between memory, body, language, and place.

D0657258712.title: Yugua Island
D0657258712.content:
“Yugua Island” (2024)
Video Installation /Sound/Color/10:36min/ 4:3

INTRODUCTION

Yugua Island (2024) is a video installation that narrates the story of sleeping/meditation/dreaming experience. Through projection, it combines the footage captured by her during a travel expedition with a sleep installation in the room, attempting to create a liminal space—exploring how the sensory world, which exists outside the objective world, weaves together illusions and real memories. At the same time, the video seeks to use minimalist visual language—one wall, one window, one bed, and two screens—to break away from the concept of linear time and space, creating a new temporal-spatial perspective that is multilayered, cyclic, and ambiguous. The video merges performance art, spatial installation, natural language, and game narrative. As the protagonist sleeps, the audience embarks on a "meditation," exploring the truth and illusion of an island sculpted by memories deep within the psyche.

N0040932085.title: Vacuum World
N0040932085.content:
“Vacuum World” (2021-2024)
Photo Series, Digital and Film, 24 Images




INTRODUCTION

In the chaotic material world, vacuum represents a state approaching the limit—an existence that is almost invisible. In a vacuum, all sound and substance are stripped away, leaving only the faintest fluctuations. We are compelled to perceive the natural presences that are "unseen and unheard."In my photo series, Vacuum World, I place the world within a vacuum-like environment, peeling away external noise to trace the emotional and material remnants submerged in everyday life—those things that are forgotten, unspoken, or never mourned.
This work attempts to critically construct a purified vacuum space outside the information-saturated modern society, in order to explore the most essential—yet faint and unseen—connections between matter and nature.

X0211275812.title: Oasis
X0211275812.content:
“Oasis” (2024)
Photo Series, Digital, 35 Images



INTRODUCTION
 
Through my photography series The Oasis, I document the growth and breath of plants, hot springs, glaciers, mist, land, and dew. I aim to awaken our sensitivity to the natural world and invite viewers into my sensory world — a non-anthropocentric symbiotic space where we can rethink the relationships between natural entities and ecosystems.
